text.p: Some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- S-E-Banken's new managing director Jacob Wallenberg is off to a roaring start, picking a new board from the Wallenberg-controlled sphere in Sweden.
- Sweden's Handelsbanken aims to expand in Norway. When the dust settles from the shake-up in the Norwegian financial market, Handelsbanken may be Norway's third largest bank.
- The ruling Social Democrat party and the umbrella union group, LO, marched in harmony through Stockholm's streets in a May 1 demonstration aimed against their common enemy -- the Right.

- As a major shareholder in the Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn, spokesman for the Swedish state Per Tegner critised the P&U board at the general shareholders' meeting because the company has not performed up to expectations.

- Many investors in Swedish investment funds missed the sharp upturns on the eastern European stock markets over the winter. Fund managers allowed the capital to stay in banks instead of investing in shares.

- As Jacob Wallenberg takes up the helm at S-E-Banken, a new board has also been appointed. Two have been recruited from outside the bank -- Peggy Bruzelius, head of ABB Financial Services and Anders Rydin, finance director of Investor.
